extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary XML/PDF locators; mechanism classes are bounded to membrane/copper chemistry assays actually present in local material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cu2+ complexation increases cytotoxic potency for P1/P3 cancer-cell assays, most strongly for P3, with the quantitative activity support captured in Table 1 activity records.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Phenotypic IC50 change is not by itself a direct molecular mechanism; mechanistic support comes from separate membrane/oxidation assays below.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC-labeled P1 and P3 localize to cellular membranes/organelles in cancer cells, supporting membrane interaction as cellular context.
direct_assay_types: fluorescence microscopy with MitoTracker colocalization context
mechanism_claims.limitations: FITC-labeled peptides could not be metallated, so this locator supports localization context rather than direct Cu2+-state localization.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SPR/EIS measurements show peptide binding to POPC tethered bilayers and formation of ion-conducting membrane defects, with holo forms remaining membrane disruptive.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model POPC bilayer assay, not a direct cancer-cell membrane rupture measurement.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Neutron reflectometry/diffraction locate P1/P3 and Cu2+-bound forms in lipid bilayers, supporting physical bilayer insertion/distribution differences, particularly deeper P3-Cu2+ insertion.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural bilayer model evidence; cellular consequence is inferred together with cytotoxicity assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: UV absorbance assays in vesicles containing polyunsaturated lipid support Cu2+/piscidin-associated lipid oxidation as chemical bilayer damage context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Cu2+-bound piscidin interactions with DLPC/POPG vesicles
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model vesicle oxidation assay; exact supplementary replicate/source curves were not locally recoverable beyond main XML/PDF figure caption and text.
